title: Should Luca build a local persistent memory system for Claude Code, and if so how?
decisionQuestion: Should Luca build a local persistent memory system for Claude Code, and if so which architecture, tooling, and implementation approach best serves his workflow without creating maintenance burden or toxic memory?

context.user: Luca La Rosa — senior AI-assisted delivery practitioner, uses Claude Code intensively for software development, agentic workflows, refactoring/replatforming, capability registry design, functional/technical analysis, prompt engineering, architecture, process automation
context.coreProblem: Claude Code is stateless between sessions. Decisions, failed attempts, patterns, constraints, preferences, and lessons learned are scattered across conversations, local files, and implicit memory.

existingMemorySystem.projectClaudeMd: Per-repo CLAUDE.md checked into each project (working)
existingMemorySystem.autoMemory: ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/ — MEMORY.md index + per-type .md files — this IS the existing auto-memory system already in place
existingMemorySystem.note: The auto-memory system is already partially working. The question is whether to extend it vs build a separate parallel system.

proposedSolution.name: Personal Claude Operating Memory
proposedSolution.description: Local, structured, searchable, maintainable persistent memory layer making the local environment stateful while Claude remains stateless

levels.level2: Session summaries — structured, produced at end of relevant sessions
levels.level3: Consolidated trusted memory (decisions/, lessons/, patterns/, anti-patterns/, projects/<name>/)

candidateStack.OmniMem: Potential primary memory layer — cross-session/cross-project memory, lifecycle management, contradiction detection, memory scoring
candidateStack.qmdSessions: Session archive/retrieval — converts Claude Code JSONL transcripts to readable/indexable Markdown
candidateStack.BMADStyle: Artifact-first methodology — explicit state, decision logs, handoff, checklists, gates
candidateStack.CodebaseMemory: Structural memory of large codebases — modules, dependencies, patterns, ADRs

context.keyRisk: Toxic memory — retrieving stale, contradictory, or out-of-scope decisions as if still valid; mixing project-specific constraints with global preferences; treating experiments as consolidated decisions; failure to prune/deprecate

questionsToResolve: 2. Is it genuinely useful or risks being overengineering?
3. Which existing tools are most appropriate?
4. Is OmniMem a good choice as the primary memory layer for Claude Code?
5. Is qmd-sessions useful as a complementary session archive?
6. Should BMAD be the primary methodological layer or just a source of inspiration?
7. Does it make sense to add a knowledge graph / codebase memory, or better to defer?
8. What are the main risks of this approach?
10. What should be automated vs. manually approved?
11. How to correctly separate: global personal memory / project-specific memory / client-specific memory / experimental memory / raw session history?
12. What is the minimum viable implementation?
13. What should be deferred to a later phase?
14. What would you change in the design?
15. What approach would you recommend starting this week in a pragmatic way?
constraints: Must remain local — no cloud persistence of potentially client-sensitive context
Must not create excessive maintenance burden that displaces actual delivery work
Must not conflict with or duplicate the existing auto-memory system at ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/
Must handle multi-project, multi-client context isolation correctly
Must be gracefully degradable — if the memory system is ignored or stale, Claude Code must still function
Token cost must be managed — not every session should retrieve everything

options.name: Extend existing auto-memory system
options.description: Formalise the existing ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/ system with explicit lifecycle rules, naming conventions, and a global personal memory layer. No new external tools.

options.name: Full proposed architecture (3 levels + OmniMem + qmd-sessions + BMAD)
options.description: Build all three levels as proposed, adopt OmniMem as primary layer, qmd-sessions for archival, BMAD methodology for discipline, codebase memory layer.

options.name: Pragmatic hybrid — extend existing + selective external tools
options.description: Extend the existing auto-memory system with a formalised personal memory layer and lifecycle rules. Add qmd-sessions for session indexing (Phase 2). Defer OmniMem and codebase memory. BMAD as methodology inspiration only.

options.name: Minimal discipline — CLAUDE.md conventions only
options.description: Rely purely on CLAUDE.md (global + per-project) with stricter conventions. No new infrastructure. Accept the statefulness limitation as-is.
